name: pwm_controller
description: Parameterized PWM controller with an 8-bit programmable duty cycle and 8-bit programmable period. The module contains a synchronous free-running counter that increments on enabled clocks, wraps to zero when it reaches the programmed period, and generates a PWM output that is high when the counter value is less than duty_cycle. All state is synchronously cleared to zero when reset_n is asserted low.

fixed_assumptions: All sequential behavior is synchronous to clk.
period and duty_cycle are sampled combinationally for compare/wrap decisions each cycle; they are not internally latched.
counter_value is externally observable and reflects the current registered counter state.

feature_contracts.description: Active-low reset clears the counter and deasserts PWM output.
With reset released and enable asserted, the counter increments on each clock until wrap conditions apply.
With enable deasserted, the counter holds its current registered value while PWM output follows the compare rule.
When the enabled counter reaches the programmed period, the next enabled cycle wraps the counter to zero.
PWM output is high only when counter_value is strictly less than duty_cycle.
PWM output is low when counter_value is equal to or above duty_cycle.

functionality: Implements a programmable pulse-width modulator. When enable is high, the internal 8-bit counter increments on each rising edge of clk. If the counter reaches the programmed period value, the next enabled increment wraps the counter to zero instead of incrementing further. The pwm_out signal is asserted whenever the current counter_value is strictly less than duty_cycle, producing a variable-duty waveform over the selected period. When enable is low, the counter holds its current value. When reset_n is low, the counter and all output registers are cleared to zero.
responsibilities: Apply synchronous active-low reset to all sequential state.
Generate wrap-around behavior using the programmable period input.
Generate pwm_out from the current counter_value versus duty_cycle comparison.
Expose counter_value as an output for observation and verification.
reset_behavior: When reset_n is low, the counter state is synchronously cleared to 8'h00 and pwm_out is driven low. Upon release of reset_n, the counter resumes from zero on the next enabled clock edge.
behavior_rules: Counter updates only on rising edges of clk.
If reset_n is low at a clock edge, counter_value becomes 8'h00 regardless of enable, duty_cycle, or period.
If reset_n is high and enable is low, the counter holds its current value.
If reset_n is high, enable is high, and counter_value equals period, the next counter value shall be 8'h00.
If reset_n is high, enable is high, and counter_value is less than period, the next counter value shall be counter_value + 1.
pwm_out is a combinational function of the current registered counter_value and duty_cycle: pwm_out = 1 when counter_value < duty_cycle, otherwise 0.
If duty_cycle is 8'h00, pwm_out shall be 0 for all counter values.
If duty_cycle is greater than 8'h00, pwm_out shall be high for counter_value values in the range 0 through duty_cycle-1 inclusive.
